name: Otto's Route
beta:
The opening lead is an easy angling ramp at fourth-class level to a chockstone, then a jam crack past chiseled holds to a bolted ledge.

Next the crack widens into a squeeze chimney slot pocked with holes left by an old pipe ladder; a big cam gives security there.
overview: The historic tourist line up Independence Monument: ramp, crack and a squeeze slot with old drilled holes, a face pitch to Lunch Box Ledge, then an exposed prow to the capstone.

current.area_walk_in: A trail up the canyon leads to the foot of the monument's southeast face; from there the route is reached by traversing the base toward the tower's northwest side.
current.descent: three double-rope raps: 150 ft north off the top ledge, 60 ft after scrambling through the Time Tunnel, then 140 ft from a 3-bolt chain anchor to the ground
current.detailed_rack: Normal desert rack plus a #4-size cam, a mid-size Tri-cam for the drilled pockets on the ridge, and double ropes for the raps
current.location: Northwest face of the tower; begin up an easy ramp slanting right to a chockstone

name: Out of Arms Reach
beta: Ascend the right-hand wall of the obvious corner standing behind a big fir. Dicey easy-grade moves lead up to the initial bolt, and two more bolts take you to the top.
overview: A short three-bolt face on the right side of a corner, with a spicy start before the first clip.

current.area_walk_in: A brief, steep, eroded track fords the creek and ascends the slope to the wall's foot. Numbering runs north to south; to find route one, start at the Buoux Block and head north.
current.descent: rappel from slings on the tree
current.anchor: no anchor; slings on a tree

name: Out of Mind Experience
beta: Climb as far as the first bolt of Astral Projection, then make a longer move sideways to the bolt at the slab's outer edge before edging back toward the anchors.
overview: Runs to the initial bolt of its neighbour Astral Projection, then makes a longer rightward move to a bolt near the slab margin, finally edging leftward to the anchors. Six bolts overall.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: climb to the first bolt of Astral Projection then traverse right to the far right edge of the slab

name: Outrageous Overhang
beta: Work up the shallow corner leaning right beside Thug Route to the tree. A small rack of nuts, small cams and TCUs is all it takes.
overview: A short shallow-corner line beside Thug Route that ends at a tree belay.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: close to Thug Route

name: Walk in Fairmont Park
beta: Start beside the big roof, go around its left side, then trend up and right over the stained seep line and some ledges to the three-bolt headwall. Small gear to about a #1.5 cam supplements.
overview: A route up the lower left face that skirts a roof, crosses a stained seep line, and ends on a short bolted headwall.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: far-left section of the bottom face, next to the big overhang

name: Ozone Direct
beta: Move left beyond a bolt, then wedge your fingers up a thin crack for about forty feet; two hard fingertip laybacks are the crux.
overview: The best finish to a four-pitch route, leaving its neighbour for an intimidating slab on the buttress.

current.area_walk_in: Climb northward over slopes littered with boulders to the cliff's base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: slab left of the main Lost in Space finish, stepping past a bolt

name: Passing Lane
beta: Pull on good holds up the face to a runout leftward traverse, then step onto the low-angle upper wall and cruise to the anchors.
overview: Good holds lead up the face to an exposed, runout move left, then easier slabby rock finishes at the anchors. Leaders should be steady on the traverse.

current.descent: lower off

name: Peaches and Cream
beta:
Begin with the lowest part of Rip Curl, then move left over flakes to a flared offwidth. Expect a long fight with stacked hands and arm bars on the crux section.

Higher, the crack tightens to fist-and-hand width and gives way to a strenuous lieback and jamming stretch. Bring plenty of big gear and tape your hands.
overview: A brutal offwidth running up the tilted, insecure left edge of a big flake, close to Twister. Stacked hands and arm-bars carry you through, and the crack narrows to hand size higher before you exit it.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.
current.descent: Rap, or carry on up Twister
current.location: Opens on the lowest bit of Rip Curl, then traverses on flakes into the flared crack

name: Graceful Dancer
beta: Reach the tree belay, then pass the bolt and enter the shallow corner. From its top, edge rightward into a thin, sustained seam and belay; easier ground above lets you bail rightward.
overview: Begins with a bolt, then enters a small right-leaning corner before drifting right into a slender, sustained seam of a crack for the first pitch. Easier ground follows, with an exit rightward.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.location: from the tree belay used by Slippage

name: Trippage
beta:
Meander up a slab, round a roof by its east side with a #1.5 cam, then belay from a shelf under a shallow groove.

The groove takes two bolts; then angle up-left to a crack, follow it out, and shift over to another one. A final crack reaches easy ground, where you leave to the east.
overview: A slab leads to a roof turned near its right end, then to a belay under a shallow groove. A bolted groove, then a pair of cracks, make up the middle; the third pitch follows a crack out to easy terrain.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.location: close to Slippage, past a big recess

name: Pearl Harbor
beta: A steep slab in two pitches. The first has thin moves protected by two bolts and creative gear placements, belaying at chains; six bolts follow up the headwall, with the crux just below the top belay. Small cams add a placement low down.
overview: Two pitches on a steep slab: thin moves on mixed bolts and gear to chains above Diagonal, then six bolts up the headwall to a hard finish just under the upper anchor.

current.area_walk_in: A path drops into the gulch and climbs out the far side to the base of the wall.
current.descent: two double-rope raps of about 46 m each

name: Pigeon Perch
beta: Take the dihedral shared with North Roof, then peel off leftward where a shelf slopes and pass a lone bolt to reach a bolted anchor.
overview: Shares the North Roof corner, then breaks left from a sloping ledge past one bolt to an anchor; sparsely protected.

current.area_walk_in: A signed trail leaves the Peak View Drive lot and climbs about three-quarters of a mile, gaining roughly 400 feet, to reach the Needle and then the Thumb a little farther uphill.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Pizza Face
beta:
Start on five bolts beside Endless Crack, then take that route's second pitch to a stance next to Kite Slab.

Next, step out rightward to a bolt, climb the steeply angled slab past two further bolts to a horn under a roof, and push through the roof where a wedged block fills the slot. Finish through a chimney.
overview: Long, hard bolted face route on the J Crack slab, with a steep slab pitch and a roof exit higher up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Politicians, Priests, and Body Bags
beta: Climb a short crack, then continue on clean face rock through four bolts, finishing at twin anchors.
overview: Starts up a short crack to a ledge, then face climbs clean rock past four bolts to a two-bolt anchor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Post Office Crack
beta: A long crack system along the wall's right edge that takes five or six pitches. Head toward the large tree against the sky; the upper pitches trend left to reach it. A standard rack suffices.
overview: A classic long crack line splitting the east edge of the main wall, five or six pitches to a big tree on the horizon.

current.descent: head east on the rim to the Bowling Alley gully, down to the East Buttress, then take the rap gully (one rope) into Cracked Canyon
current.location: The lengthy crack line at the main wall's right (east) edge, aiming for a big tree on the horizon

name: Powder in the Sky
beta:
The opening pitch is a sixty-foot face section that is mostly unprotected, with a few harder moves near its top before a bolted belay.

The second pitch trends up and left over four bolts toward a distinct roof; the crux sits at the fourth bolt, and the roof is turned on its left side to a ledge with anchors.
overview: A celebrated two-pitch face climb on the Mirror Wall: a bold, sparsely protected first pitch, then a bolted second pitch past a roof.

current.descent: rap the route with two ropes
current.location: The obvious scalloped wall just east of the Queasy Street arch

name: Power Pig
beta: Begin beneath a broken corner, then trend leftward through two ring bolts into the crack system that angles rightward. Three more bolts follow, with a thin, steep crux; an extra medium cam or large wire helps in the crack under the headwall.
overview: A classic of the crag up the central shield: ring bolts lead to a right-angling crack and a thin, steep finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Beneath a fractured right-facing corner in the middle of the main shield

name: Prince of Thieves
beta: Start near a big Douglas fir and follow the bolts through a pair of roofs, finishing alongside the V-shaped slot on its right-hand edge.
overview: Bolts lead over a pair of roofs and up the right edge of a V-shaped slot.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 10 ft right of the big Douglas fir

name: Project X
beta: Straight up the wall centre on five bolts, ending at a lone anchor at the wall's top.
overview: A stiff five-bolt line through the middle of the wall the sector is named for.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Straight up the center of the wall

name: Northeast Ridge
beta: From the saddle at about 13,000 ft, follow the ridge crest and ledges on its right side. Near 13,300 ft the route crosses a small gap in the ridge, the "leap of faith" - a short step across rather than a true leap - onto narrow, exposed ledges beyond. Around 13,400 ft you reach a steep band of greenish rock (the "green wall"); climb it on Class 3-4 ledges, testing every hold. Above, the route works up a series of gullies and ledges on the west side of the ridge, marked by cairns; staying on the cairned line keeps the difficulty at Class 3-4, while wandering usually lands you on steeper, looser ground. Above about 13,900 ft the angle eases and you walk to the summit. Note landmarks on the way up, because the upper route is easy to lose on the way down.
overview: The standard route on Pyramid Peak climbs from Maroon Lake into the amphitheater under the north face, up a steep scree slope to a saddle on the northeast ridge, then weaves across exposed ledges and gullies to the summit. It is one of the most serious standard routes on a Colorado fourteener: short on distance but sustained, exposed and built of notoriously loose rock. Expect constant route-finding and real consequences for a slip or a dropped rock.

current.approach: From Maroon Lake Trailhead, take the Crater Lake trail about 1.5 miles to a junction near 10,100 ft and turn left onto the Pyramid Peak trail. It climbs steeply through forest to the entrance of the amphitheater below Pyramid's north face at about 11,200 ft, where the maintained trail ends. Cross the rock glacier in the amphitheater on a faint, cairned path, then climb the steep scree and dirt slope, roughly 1,000 ft of gain, to the saddle on the northeast ridge at about 13,000 ft.
current.descent: Descend the same route, reversing the ledges, gullies, green wall and ridge gap back to the saddle, then down the steep scree slope to the amphitheater. Go slowly: the loose terrain is more dangerous going down, and the cairned line is easy to miss from above.

name: Quintet
beta:
A zigzagging crack-and-corner line that bends over five roofs. Begin from a flake on the right and step left where the largest roof hangs; protection runs from small wires up to medium cams.

The next pitch ascends the dihedral and crosses a roof on a fist-sized crack.
overview: Crack and corner climb up a zigzagging corner (facing right) that pulls over five small roofs; a second pitch takes a fist crack through a roof at 5.10d.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: A mixed rack from small wires up to mid-size cams

name: Quiver and Quill
beta: Follow a hand crack that leans, out at the westernmost end of the formation. Cams up to about 3.5 inches cover it.

current.area_walk_in: From the end of the road, a short trail climbs to the saddle between Turkey Rock and the Turkey Perch. Turkey Tail is the buttress off to the north (left) of the Perch, reached by crossing a talus field.
current.descent: rappel 23 m from bolts on the west edge of the belay ledge
current.location: leaning hand crack at the western extreme of the rock, facing the neighbouring Perch

name: Radiation Control Area
beta: Thin, technical climbing on the wall's right side where reach matters. Above the roof the crux relies on tiny pebble pinches. Four bolts lead to lowering anchors on cold shuts.
overview: A thin, technical four-bolt line whose hardest moves pinch pebbles above a roof; reach matters.

current.descent: lower off
current.location: On the right-hand side of the wall

name: Rainbow Bridge
beta: Begin with an easy 5.6 crack that ends on a flake, then pull up through a sequence of pockets past a handful of old fixed pegs. It is somewhat runout, so expect to lean on the fixed gear.
overview: Steep pothole pulling, somewhat runout, up the wall beside the big arching overhang; a short easy crack gains a flake, then fixed pegs protect the upper face.

current.descent: two-rope rappel from the tree-ledge anchors
current.anchor: fixed anchors on a tree ledge
current.location: right beside the big arching roof near the parking area; begin up a brief 5.6 crack, reaching a flake top

name: Rainbow Wall
beta: Scramble up the ramp, then angle leftward on 5.9 ground to the first bolt. The difficulty builds steadily to a tricky crux past the fourth bolt, after which easier climbing reaches the ridge. Carry some wires and a #1 cam for the start.
overview: A sustained, increasingly hard bolted face pitch up a colorful vertical wall on Wind Tower's south side, with a tricky crux above the fourth bolt and easier ground up onto the southwest ridge.

current.area_walk_in: Step across the plank footbridge spanning South Boulder Creek, then follow the path leading eastward beneath the south face.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: low on the southern side, left of a ramp that tilts steeply rightward

name: Renaissance Wall
beta: A lengthy bolted face climb with sustained difficulty up the steep right-hand side of the gully, in three pitches. Begin high in the chimney below a curving crack; about eight quickdraws are enough.
overview: Long, sustained bolted face route on the steep chasm side next to Isis Buttress.

current.descent: Double-rope rappels
current.location: Sheer right-hand side of the chasm west of Isis Buttress, about 400 ft up its chimney, below a crack curving up left

name: Right Center
beta: From the neighbouring route's rappel station, trend rightward through a series of dihedrals past scattered fixed gear to a belay below a black groove. Follow that groove to the top; it is runout.

current.area_walk_in: A signed trail leaves the Peak View Drive lot and climbs about three-quarters of a mile, gaining roughly 400 feet, to reach the Needle and then the Thumb a little farther uphill.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Roughly 20 ft right of the Left Center pillar (or step right from the Pin Job rap anchor)

name: Rim Job
beta: Begin back of a fir tree, to the right of the large dihedral, then crank up and rightward past six bolts to double cold-shut anchors. Holds are mostly good, but reaching the anchors without a dynamic lunge to the ridge is awkward.
overview: A standout of the canyon: six bolts up a steeply overhanging arete on mostly good holds.

current.area_walk_in: A brief, steep, eroded track fords the creek and ascends the slope to the wall's foot. Numbering runs north to south; to find route one, start at the Buoux Block and head north.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Road Kill
beta: Climb a three-bolt slab to a ledge, then move straight to a mantle that lands you at a rest above a roof. Haul over the large roof on big holds and finish via another bulge, or angle right for an easier exit. Ten bolts in all.
overview: Billed as a great route. A three-bolt slab leads to a ledge, then a mantle gives access to a rest above a roof. The big roof is crossed on jugs and another bulge, or an easier line to the right, finishes it.

current.descent: lower off
current.location: Begins on a short three-bolt slab below the ledge that slants up to the right, or scramble that ledge from its right end

name: Road Warrior
beta: An easy slab leads to a corner beneath the large roof. Grab a rest there, then power through the roof, where several separate 5.12 cruxes await on fine rock. Ten bolts total.
overview: From a ledge belay, easy slab climbing leads to a corner under the big roof; rest there, then fight through a sequence of hard moves over the overhang on excellent rock.

current.descent: lower off

name: Lucky Seven
beta: The big dihedral resembles a numeral 7. Climb up it and then get around the roof by going left. Gear to about five inches is wanted.
overview: Named for its dihedral, which is shaped like the numeral seven. Follow it up, then turn the roof out left.

current.descent: walk northward
current.location: the big left-facing dihedral low on Rock One

name: Rocket Fuel
beta: Steep slab work with one hard smear move opens the route, then the upper headwall is somewhat easier; the pitch ends on a narrow ledge with anchors.
overview: Steep slab with one hard smearing move, then a 5.10b headwall leading to a narrow anchored ledge.

current.descent: rappel; a single rope is too short to get down from the ledge

name: Rooster Tail
beta: An arching crack up the left edge of the wall. Near the top, step back leftward onto a finger-sized crack for the crux; a 3.5 cam is useful.
overview: An arching crack that finishes with a leftward finger crack.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Curving crack running along the extreme left of the face

name: Root Canal
beta: Follow the first hundred feet of the neighbouring route and belay, then leave it leftward and ascend the slab via two bolts, curving back to the right.
overview: A slab variation off Cleft Palate, passing two bolts beside a slanting roof.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Follow Cleft Palate for its first 100 ft, then head out left

name: Rotten Teeth
beta:
A long buttress route of fourteen pitches. Early pitches climb unprotected slab and cracks; the fourth heads leftward on a very thin crack through a steep headwall, then a thin bolted slab to a groove.

Upper pitches follow grooves, a good left-facing corner and slab leading into a system of cracks, mostly at 5.8 to 5.9.
overview: The longest route on Big Rock, a runout journey up the northern buttress mixing a thin crack, a left-facing corner and long friction slabs.

current.location: northern (left) buttress; the old start just left of the lowest toe was wiped out, so begin in the gully to its left

name: Rush
beta: Start like the neighbouring route, but veer off rightward at the first bolt, get past a burly bulge, and layback through a roof. At the final bolt, choose either anchor. Five bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the obvious trail south from the lot, then drop around the formation through a notch and down a gully. If the ground begins to feel like fifth class, you have gone too far.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: shares its opening moves with the neighbouring line, then veers right at the first clip

name: Secrets Of Nature
beta: A three-bolt line up the vertical face to the right of the neighbouring route. Clip the first bolt with a stick, carry small gear for the upper section, and belay on that route's ledge.
overview: A hard three-bolt wall to the right of Javelin, finishing on small gear to the Javelin ledge. Stick-clip the first bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Find the climbers' trail through the forest and up the steep talus slope, heading for the canyon just right of the main wall. Loose rock is common, so avoid kicking stones down onto others.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Vertical face just right of Javelin

name: Shadow of a Hangdog (aka Fat Fingers)
beta: A layback section and thin crack in the line east of the arete. Nuts and small cams protect it, and it is easily toproped from the anchors of Brain Cloud.
overview: A pleasant layback sequence leading into a thin crack on the arete's right flank. It is easy to set up a toprope from the anchors of a neighbouring route.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on the arete's right flank

name: Shake 'n' Bake
beta:
Start along the left edge of the big flake leaning on the face; a few moves of 5.9 on crumbly flakes lead onto a gentle, runout slab and bolted belay on top of the flake.

The second pitch follows the water streak clipping a series of bolts to a stance under a small roof. Add a short hand-crack third pitch, with gear to 3 inches, to reach the summit.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: rap 165 ft with two ropes, or finish over a short hand crack to the summit
current.location: the flake's left edge, where it rests against the wall

name: Room With a View
beta: From the gully, go up an easy chimney, exit rightward onto an angled ledge system and belay there. The route itself follows the colorful yellow wall overhead, clipping five bolts to the lowering anchors.
overview: An excellent bolted line up a beautiful yellow wall high in the gully, reached after climbing an easy chimney.

current.area_walk_in: Climb northward over slopes littered with boulders to the cliff's base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
